newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thailand appoints former SEC chief as key adviser.
newsitem.headline: Thailand appoints former SEC chief as key adviser.

text.p: Thailand's new Finance Minister Amnuay Viravan said on Tuesday he had appointed the former head of the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC), Ekamol Khiriwat, as the head of his team of economic advisors.
"Ekamol will oversee the money, capital and foreign exchange markets," said Amnuay.
The former regulator was not available for comment.
Ekamol was forced to quit the SEC and dismissed from his concurrent job as deputy governor of the Bank of Thailand last December by former Finance Minister Surakiart Sathirathai.
The former regulator had been accused of leaking confidential information, a charge he has denied.

Last week, the Attorney General dropped legal charges filed by the government against Ekamol and said the finance ministry and other plaintiffs had failed to reveal witnesses or provide enough evidence to back up the charges.
